summary:
P1.4c needs-review (NO code committed): the task's named enforcement point is verified DEAD code, so gating it would close CG-4 for zero live paths and would NOT satisfy the demand completion definition ("CG-4 across all submission paths"). The correct enforcement point is outside the named scope and changes visible behavior -> controller decision required.

VERIFIED GROUND TRUTH (independent 2-pass grep + call-site reads, Node not needed):
- Finding 1: GatewayActionRegistry.ts candidate:create (:24-29) + recipe:create (:77-82) have NO live dispatcher. Whole-repo scan: the only live `req.gw(...)` Gateway dispatch is 'guard_rule:create' (guardRules.ts:185); candidate:create/recipe:create appear only as the 2 register() defs + 1 docstring (gatewayMiddleware.ts:31); buildGatewayRequest (:221) is never called; no dynamic ${resource}:create reaches them. Of 31 registered gateway actions only guard_rule:create is dispatched -> the knowledge/recipe create-action layer is vestigial (V3 unified Candidate+Recipe; creates moved to direct service calls). Gating these two = real-caller-less glue code.
- Finding 2: the REAL live main-body knowledge-create entries BYPASS the Gateway: (a) lib/cli/AiScanService.ts:159 knowledgeService.create(recipe) -- the in-process AI producer (authors via embedded AlembicAgent runScanAgentTask extract, then create+publish; only Core stage-3, no stage-1/2), live via bin/cli.ts:1210; this is the genuine main-body CG-4 in-process gap and exactly the 'independent knowledgeService.create' path design §C.7 told us to re-point ('若独立，P1.4 增显式 re-point'). (b) lib/http/routes/knowledge.ts:186 POST /api/v1/knowledge, live via HttpServer.ts:307 -- external HTTP. The task's named line numbers are a stale pointer (P0.0 oracle recorded the dead Gateway regs as the independent-create site).
- Finding 3: REUSE of AlembicAgent runInProcessRecipeAuthoringGate is impossible without touching AlembicAgent (forbidden): it lives only in AlembicAgent/src/tools/runtime/handlers/{recipeAuthoringGate,knowledge}.ts and is NOT re-exported from any @alembic/agent public subpath. Sanctioned fallback (own §C.11 fs resolver, byte-faithful, consuming @alembic/core/knowledge validateAgainst/resolveAuthoringProfile) is ready -- not the blocker.

OPTIONS: A (recommended) re-aim gate to the live independent create AiScanService.ts:159 (§C.7 intent), opportunistic profile (content+cheap grounding, no 3-file floor/session-scope), producer-prompt-first already satisfied via embedded AlembicAgent insightProducer (P1.4b); closes the real CG-4 in-process gap. B also gate external HTTP knowledge.ts:186 = public-contract visible-behavior change, high should-pass risk -> separate USER gate. C implement literal task (gate the 2 dead Gateway actions) as defense-in-depth = matches named scope+acceptance but closes zero live paths and leaves AiScanService open -> does NOT satisfy CG-4-all-paths; low value alone. Recommend A (+optionally C); B separate user decision. Ready to implement A immediately on confirmation. Full evidence + options in ledger doc.

risks: Premise conflict: the task package + P0.0 oracle name the two Gateway create actions as a live in-process entry, but they are dead. Following the literal instruction yields a green acceptance test on a path nobody calls -> a misleading 'CG-4 complete' signal. This is the blocker that makes the result needs-review, not completed.

If controller picks Option A: gating AiScanService.ts:159 changes the visible behavior of the `alembic ai-scan` CLI (newly-rejects low-quality recipes -- bounded content/cheap-grounding tightening). Will deliver the currently-passing-corpus new-reject set at impl. STOP-if-should-pass-rejected discipline applies.
If Option B: tightening POST /api/v1/knowledge changes a public HTTP API accept contract for human/dashboard/API clients (high should-pass risk) -> likely a USER gate, not just controller.
Option C alone (literal gate on dead actions) leaves CG-4 open for the live AiScanService path while turning the acceptance green -> do not accept C as CG-4 closure.

Reuse impossibility (Finding 3) means a 3rd in-process fs-resolver copy will exist in main-body (host plugin + AlembicAgent + main-body); §12.5 parity test mitigates by asserting same-resolver host-vs-in-process equality; a future Core-exported reference resolver could de-dup (out of scope).
